text:
Maya: FYI support ticket from AcmeCorp — multiple 504s and timeouts on hosted /v1/generate since ~09:10 UTC. Customer says errors spike after a churn of small chat requests.
Diego: Can you paste their example request + headers?
Maya: Pasted below (removed API key). They report 30–50 rps of tiny messages (<= 20 tokens), concurrency ~40 per tenant.
Maya: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","input":"hi","max_tokens":16}'```
Priya: Thanks — sounds like continuous-batching backlog. Small requests tend to get aggregated and we hit queue depth defaults. Any stack traces or gateway logs?
Maya: Support attached gateway logs (I trimmed):
Maya: ```
> 2026-03-17T09:09:58Z gateway request_id=abc123 tenant=acmecorp downstream_enqueue_ms=32000 status=504 message="request timed out waiting for worker"
> 2026-03-17T09:10:02Z gateway request_id=abc128 tenant=acmecorp queue_depth=98 batcher=continuous backlog_ms=27500
> 2026-03-17T09:10:04Z gateway request_id=abc129 tenant=acmecorp worker_kv_miss=true model=rw-1.1 quant=8bit
```
Sam: queue_depth=98 is very high — defaults are 100. If multiple tenants or large KV-cache cold starts, continuous batcher can stall.
Priya: We also recently changed the batcher max_wait_ms to 50 in canary for low-latency mode; that can cause more frequent small batches but shouldn't saturate queue depth — unless dequeue throughput is reduced due to worker GC or high kernel contention.
Diego: @Priya can you check worker-side metrics (serving runtime p95 token latency, active kv cache misses) for the affected pool?
Priya: Looking now — runtime p95 token-latency jumped from 6ms to 120ms across pool-3 at 09:09. KV-cache cold misses spiked; evictions also rose. Worker CPU shows tail CPU spikes aligning with 09:08–09:11.
Maya: Customer also noted auth retries around the same time (we saw 2xx then immediate 401 then 5xx) — could be client side replays increasing load.
Sam: Could be a retry storm. Any client-side retry policy in the ticket?
Maya: They use default SDK retry (3 retries on 5xx) with backoff disabled for dev.
Diego: That would amplify the pileup. Immediate mitigation options: 1) apply tenant-level rate limit clamp for AcmeCorp, 2) temporarily route tenant to lower-cost model variant with smaller kv footprint, 3) bump queue_depth for pool-3, 4) disable sync retries (ask customer).
Priya: Short-term I'd recommend 1 + 2. We can bump queue_depth but that risks longer tail timeouts. Also we should increase worker count for pool-3 by +2 nodes if capacity available.
Maya: I've asked AcmeCorp to enable exponential backoff and drop retries for a few minutes. They're okay with a short throttle.
engbot: Automated action: applied tenant rate limit 40rps for tenant=acmecorp at 09:12 UTC (rule id=rl-942).
Diego: Good. Priya — can you spin 2 additional workers and temporarily route acmecorp to rw-1.1-small?
Priya: Spinning workers now. Routing policy change in progress: routing acmecorp -> rw-1.1-small variant (reduced KV footprint). ETA ~45s.
Maya: Customer confirms errors dropped after 09:14 — still seeing occasional 504s but far fewer.
Sam: Can you capture timeline graphs: gateway queue depth, worker p95, KV miss rate, tenant request rate, retries? We'll need that for postmortem.
Priya: Saving metrics dash. Early view: queue_depth fell from ~98 to ~12 within 90s of rate limit + routing change. Worker p95 back to ~8ms. KV miss rate reduced by ~70%.
Diego: Next steps: 1) postmortem draft, include customer repro and SDK retry behavior, 2) consider default SDK change to enable jittered backoff, 3) add tenant admission control flag to auto-detect repeated small-message spikes and trigger backpressure or model fallback, 4) investigate why GC/kernel contention hit pool-3 — could be a kernel selection regression from the last runtime bump.
Maya: I'll log the support ticket update and confirm customer is stable.
Sam: Please attach the curl repro and a small load script we used to repro locally (cc Priya).
Priya: Repro steps I used locally: `hey -n 2000 -c 40 -q 0.5 -m POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","input":"hi","max_tokens":12}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — this recreates queue growth in ~30s when SDK retries are aggressive.
Diego: Good. I'll own the postmortem. Assigning to eng-runtime, eng-sre, and devex for SDK changes.
Maya: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up once the customer confirms stable for 2 hours. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Incident triage created: INC-2026-1489 assigned -> eng-runtime, priority=P2
Diego: If customer still sees tail 504s after config changes we should consider rolling back the recent batcher param change in canary.
Priya: Noted — I'll prepare a rollback playbook and runbook entries for continuous-batcher saturation scenarios.
Maya: End of thread — will update INC record with timeline and attach logs.
